items.title: Lights-out Luka and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
items.summary: It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contendersOne of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished.But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two top records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more. Continue reading...

items.title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
items.summary: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford BridgeLiam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer.On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place. Continue reading...

items.title: GTA in Istanbul? Meet the game developers bringing virtual crime chaos to their home cities
items.summary: From Helsinki to Istanbul, independent developers are putting Grand Theft Auto-style action on their home streets, and without billion-dollar budgets. They tell us how they do itLike most kids who shouldn’t have been playing Grand Theft Auto III in 2001, Eamonn Swayah imagined a version of Rockstar Games’ groundbreaking criminal sandbox set in his own back yard. In his case, that was a Manchester council estate, complete with local accents, driving on the left, and plenty of ways to hustle.He didn’t know it, but swapping the game’s facsimile of early 2000s New York City for a different setting was an idea he shared with many watchful game developers. Rockstar’s 3D open world template, it turned out, could be plonked in just about any location, so long as it had people and enough cars to run them over with. After GTA III attracted immense commercial success (and controversy), dozens of copycats and spiritual sequels hit the market throughout the 00s and 2010s. items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
items.summary: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against BrentfordNottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. items.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
items.summary: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser.The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

items.title: Javokhir Sindarov hangs on for draw in first real fight of world title match
items.summary: Third straight draw leaves title match at 1½–1½Sindarov drops to eight seconds on move 39Gukesh Dommaraju plays white after first rest dayAll your Gukesh v Sindarov questions, answeredAfter two quieter draws, the world chess championship came to life on Thursday as Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov came within eight seconds of sudden death before fighting back to split the point with India’s Gukesh Dommaraju after nearly five hours. Their spirited 60-move battle at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in the Geneva suburbs left their $2.5m match level at 1½–1½ heading into the first rest day.Gukesh, playing with the black pieces, returned to the Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez, the opening he used in Tuesday’s 38-move opener. The defending champion sprang the first surprise on move five (5 … Be7), bringing out his bishop before retreating the knight that had taken Sindarov’s e-pawn, putting the challenger behind on time for the first time in the match. After 15 moves, Gukesh still had nearly 1hr 58min of his starting two hours, almost 40 minutes more than his opponent. Continue reading...

items.title: Slow internet? The best wifi extenders and mesh systems to boost your home network – tested
items.summary: We put 11 range extenders and mesh systems to the test to find the fastest and most reliable for streaming, gaming and working from home• The best office chairsFast fibre broadband is fantastic – if the wifi signal reaches the part of your home where you need it. Most of us use the router provided by our broadband provider, often tucked away in a hallway or corner of the lounge. Sadly, these often don’t have the range to cover every room in your home, leaving you high and dry when you’re trying to binge-watch TV or get work done in a distant home office.Wifi extenders and mesh systems can help. Extenders plug in to a mains socket between your location and the router, then pass data backwards and forwards to extend your router’s reach. Mesh systems are even smarter, pairing a secondary router with one or two satellite units, which work together to extend the wifi coverage throughout your home. The mesh system can pass your connection from unit to unit to make sure you’re always getting the best possible link from your device to the internet, wherever you are in your home. Continue reading...

items.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
items.summary: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts“I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.”It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil. Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United, whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. items.title: Dressmaker review – delightful business sim is a cut above
items.summary: PC; Cosy Lives/Free LivesCatering to the exacting whims of a small town preparing for some grand visitors presents absorbing, beautifully designed – and surprisingly thrilling – challengesThe small town of Twillford is abuzz with intrigue and excitement. A local duke has died and ladies of a certain standing are determined to make an impression at the funeral. As a newly arrived dressmaker with the only clothing shop in the area, you’re about to get plenty of work.Thus begins this utterly delightful sim game, in which you talk to customers, gather their style preferences and tailor specific outfits just for them. It could be a suitably respectful funeral frock, with just a hint of style to catch the eye of the duke’s wealthy relatives, or perhaps a work outfit for a farmer who loves bright colours. Once you have your brief, you open your sketchbook and draft a pattern using fabric swatches and a pencil to colour in your design. Need something elegant? How about a strapless bodice. An outfit for the office? A pencil skirt is a good call. Continue reading...
